question: 'Ratnavali' was written by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harsha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ratnavali:

 
 
• Ratnavali is a renowned Sanskrit play written by Harshavardhan, a prominent ruler of northern India during the 7th century.
 
• The play is a romantic comedy that showcases the literary prowess of Harshavardhan and his contribution to Indian literature.
 
• Harshavardhan, also known as Harsha, was not only a great king but also a notable writer and patron of arts and culture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Premchand**

 
 
• The original name of Munshi Premchand was Dhanpat Rai Srivastava.
 
• He was an Indian writer famous for his modern Hindustani literature.
 
• Munshi Premchand is one of the most celebrated writers of the Indian subcontinent and is regarded as one of the foremost Hindi writers of the early twentieth century.
 
• He published his first collection of five short stories in 1907 in a book called Soz-e Watan.
 
• He began writing under the pen name "Nawab Rai", but subsequently switched to "Premchand", Munshi being an honorary prefix.
 
• His novels include Godaan, Karmabhoomi, Gaban, Mansarovar, Idgah. 
 
• Premchand was commemorated with the issue of a special 30 Paise postage stamp by India Post on 31 July 1980.
 
 
 
• **​Surdas**
 
 
• The Bhakti poet from Agra is considered to be born between 1478 and 1483.
 
• Surdas was blind from birth and lived on the banks of the Yamuna river.
 
• He was the disciple of Vallabha Acharya.
 
• Surdas was a worshipper of Lord Krishna.
 
• He wrote poems in Brajbhasa in praise of Krishna.
 
• His composition Sur Sagar contains descriptions of Krishna.
